cadence: weekly, Monday before the US open
method: Every Monday each open call is re-examined against the claims its note made. The numbers are computed from the record: where the call stands against what the note called for, how far the stop is, and a price-only range for where it can finish, drawn from the position's own recent volatility with no view assumed. The verdict is a judgment, stated with dated evidence: each claim the note relied on is re-measured and marked as holding or not, and the verdict has to follow from those marks. A broken thesis closes the call on the Scorecard from the review date. The return a note called for is written once and never changed.

latest.book_now: After this review the book is four calls, all with a physical constraint or a policy actor behind them: long US natural gas against war-priced oil (the oil-to-gas extreme has been closing from the oil side, gas has held its gain), short wheat through the fund with money-manager length still at a record, long the yen at the month-two retest of the July intervention, and a long euro that is under water but whose driver — record euro shorts — is still in place. Two calls come off today. The bank-versus-Nasdaq pair is closed: what has moved it is a rates shock the note said it was not built on, and the volatility-curve reading it was built on is gone. The TIPS-versus-Treasuries pair is closed because it worked: the gap between gold and the inflation breakeven that the note was built on has closed, three-quarters of the widening it called for has printed, and what is left is not worth carrying a duration mismatch through a 10-year yield at 5.29%. Highest conviction: natural gas and wheat, each within a point or two of what its note called for with the driver intact. Lowest: the euro, which needs the dollar to give back its September gain inside six weeks. A reader holding the earlier calls takes off the bank pair and the TIPS pair at the review date's close and leaves the other four alone.

calls.title: Two prices for the same insurance, and only one of them is cheap
calls.called_for_basis: the +12 basis point six-month median widening in the note's base rate, turned into a return at the legs' entry duration (about eight years)
calls.expected_basis: the current mark (+0.17%) plus the 3 basis points of widening still outstanding against the +12bp base rate, at the entry duration of about eight years
calls.view_now: This one is closed because it worked, not because it failed. The note was built on gold and the breakeven pricing inflation differently; gold has fallen 3.4% and the breakeven has widened 9 of the 12 basis points the base rate called for, and the gap is gone. What the pair has to show for it is +0.17%, because a general rise in yields hurts the longer-duration TIPS leg more than the Treasury leg. With the driver resolved, what is left is roughly 3 basis points of expected widening carried through a 10-year at 5.29% and real yields at their three-year high — a duration mismatch with no edge attached. We take the result.
calls.action_reason: The mispricing the note identified has closed. Closed at the review date's close on the Scorecard; the remaining expected gain is a few basis points and the rates market is too violent to carry a duration mismatch for it.

calls.title: The volatility curve is at its steepest in five years. That has been a pay cut, not a warning.
calls.called_for_basis: the note's conditional median for banks against the S&P over six months after a bottom-5% volatility-curve reading (37 episodes, 60% hit rate)
calls.expected_basis: the current mark (−10.3%) plus the note's own unconditional median for a random bank-versus-index entry (−1.4% over six months) — there is no conditioning edge left to add
calls.view_now: The call was built on a volatility-curve reading that has since gone back to mid-range, and the ten points it has lost came from something the note explicitly said it was not built on: a rates shock that has taken the 10-year to 5.29% and hit banks harder than the index it is short. The base rate offered a median gain of under four points at a 60% hit rate; from ten points under water that edge does not reach back to even. We no longer expect this call to pan out. Banks may well recover once rates settle, but that would be a different call with a different reason, and it should be written as one.
calls.action_reason: The reason for the position is gone and what is moving it is a risk the note ruled out of scope. Closed at the review date's close on the Scorecard; a reader holding it takes it off rather than waiting four and a half months for a mechanism that is no longer in play.

driver_checks.claim: The relative leg is a volatility-structure trade: banks against the index respond to the steep volatility curve, not to a rates or credit shock, which the note listed as the risk it was not built on.

driver_checks.now: 10-year Treasury 5.29% and the 10-year real yield 2.93%, both at the 100th percentile of the last three years; 2-year 4.88%; banks are down 10.0% since entry against the Nasdaq up 0.3% and the S&P down 1.3% — the move is a rates repricing, not the volatility mechanism

calls.title: The most one-sided trade in the market is not on any chart
calls.called_for_basis: the note's base rate: median three-month euro return after speculative euro positioning at or below the 15th percentile (77% positive, 26 weeks)
calls.expected_basis: the current mark (−1.66%) plus roughly half the base-rate three-month median (+3.18%) for the six weeks left, with the euro reading still inside the condition
calls.view_now: The euro side of the setup is still there: speculators remain near a record short and hedgers near a record long, and that is the base rate the call is graded on. The dollar side has gone against us in the one way the note said it could — real yields have surged, the dollar index is up 1.5% and speculators have used the rally to halve their long rather than being forced out of it. The pair is down 1.7% with six weeks left and the stop at 103 on the dollar index is 1.5% away. We still expect the euro to recover from here, but not enough inside the horizon to reach what the note called for.
calls.action_reason: The base rate the call is marked on still applies and the stop has not printed, so the position stays on through its horizon. It is the lowest-conviction call in the book and is sized as one.

calls.called_for_basis: the note's base rate between its one-month (−5.3%) and three-month (−6.6%) medians for a two-month horizon, taken as a short return
calls.expected_basis: the note's three-month base-rate median (−6.6% on wheat, 13 of 16 negative) taken as a short return, with the driver reading unchanged
calls.view_now: The driver is unchanged: fund length in wheat is still at a record and has not begun to come out, and wheat has drifted 3% lower while the fund the note told the reader to short has fallen 5.7%. That is most of what the base rate called for, five weeks in, with the stop at 767 more than 10% away. The remaining edge is the difference between the one-month and three-month medians — a further point or so — plus the fund's own drag when the curve is steep.
calls.action_reason: Driver intact, most of the move earned, stop far away. It runs to its early-November horizon.

calls.title: Oil carries a war premium. US natural gas carries none.
calls.called_for_basis: the note's base rate: median front-month gas gain over three months after an oil-to-gas ratio reading at or above the 95th percentile (42 episodes since 2004)
calls.expected_basis: the note's base-rate median (+7.6% over three months) plus a modest allowance for the ratio still sitting at the 90th percentile with funds at a record short; the sub-sample where oil had already rallied 10% into the reading gives +5.0%, which the position has passed
calls.view_now: This is doing exactly what the base rate said an extreme of this kind does: the ratio is coming in from both sides, with oil giving up 11% and gas holding a 7% gain — most of the +7.6% the note called for, three weeks into a thirteen-week horizon. The extended fund short in gas is still there, which is fuel for the leg we own. The ratio is no longer at the 95th percentile, so the remaining edge is smaller than at entry; the position keeps its gain with a stop 19% away.
calls.action_reason: Driver intact and the mechanism is working as described. It runs to its December horizon; the note's own sizing already treats it as a three-month trade, not a winter hold.

calls.title: The record yen rescue looks dead. So did the last three at exactly this point.
calls.called_for_basis: the note's target: 147 on dollar-yen by late January 2027, the median months-two-to-six move applied from 157.34, roughly +6% on the fund
calls.expected_basis: the note's base rate unchanged: the median months-two-to-six move in dollar-yen after an intervention campaign (−6.9%), which is roughly +6% on the fund before costs
calls.view_now: Eight sessions in and flat, which is what month two looked like in every prior campaign. The authorities have not withdrawn their stated readiness to intervene, the BoJ has just raised rates, and dollar-yen is sitting exactly where the call entered. Nothing has been tested yet; the tests are the 2 October jobs report and any sign the authorities have stepped back. Three prior episodes is a thin record, as the note said, and one counterexample would change the median.
calls.action_reason: Nothing has changed since publication; the call is one week into a four-month horizon with the driver in place.
